newsitem.title: USA: New DOT head seen winning Senate confirmation.
newsitem.headline: New DOT head seen winning Senate confirmation.

text.p: President Clinton's choice for Transportation Secretary, Rodney Slater, is seen sailing through Senate confirmation hearings on Wednesday with only a little critical questioning, sources said.

The questions will likely center on his extensive travels as administrator of the Federal Highway Administration, the post he now holds and his lack of a background in aviation, the department's high-profile agency.
But Congressional and industry sources said Clinton's long time Arkansas ally will be approved by the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Commitee and the full Senate.
When Clinton was Arkansas governor, he named Slater to the state highway commission and later as its chairman, the first black to serve in that post.
When Clinton became president, he brought Slater to Washington to head the highway administration, where he logged in 300,000 miles of business travel, visiting 40 states.
Committee sources said it was likely that Slater would be quizzed on the costs of his travels, but could if he would asked if the travels were linked to any fund-raising.

Aviation industry sources said questions would likely be asked about Slater's lack of a background in aviation -- the second largest unit of the department in funds spent, after the highway unit, but a center of high interest because of recent airlines crashes.

His predecessor as Transportation Secretary was Federico Pena, who was not an aviation expert, but became deeply involved in aviation as mayor of Denver when the city $4.9 billion airport was being built.
